$comment: A correct answer wrapped in prose and a fenced block, which is the shape a chatty vendor returns however
plainly the prompt asks for JSON only. The parser has to find it, because an unparseable reply is an
environment failure and a correct answer reported as one would hide a run that worked.
A frozen copy of one case of the live corpus and of the menu it is scored against. The pair (expected, menu)
is the whole input to scoreCase beside the reply, so both are stored here rather than read live: a replay has
to keep scoring the scenario it was derived against after the corpus moves on, and
npm run test:eval-routing-data already holds the live corpus against the shipped menu.

expected.rationale: The deliverable is the user's own understanding rather than an artifact, which is the only item on the menu that is true of.

derivation: parseRouting tries the fenced candidates before the bare text, so the block between the fences parses and the
route/TMT/bmad-teach-me-testing matches the oracle, so routeCorrect is true.
decidingTokens is [learn, fundamental] and the reason carries "learn" and "fundamentals" under the prefix rule,
so tokensFound is 2 of 2. The oracle names no scope, so scopeTokens is 0 and scopeOk stays false without
counting against anything: the harness only takes a scope opportunity where the fixture declares one.

answer.reason: the deliverable is that you learn testing from the fundamentals up rather than any artifact
